source_artifacts.command: python -m src.pipeline.step3.train_fusion --dataset ton_iot --use-head-logits --output-dir data/ton_iot/processed/step3_fusion_head && python -m src.pipeline.step4.train_feedback --dataset ton_iot --use-llm-head --top-k-percent 15.0 --agaf-benchmark-path data/ton_iot/processed/step3_fusion_head/benchmark_summary.json --output-dir data/ton_iot/processed/step4_feedback_head15 && python -m src.pipeline.step4.assemble_ladder --dataset ton_iot --use-llm-head --fusion-dir data/ton_iot/processed/step3_fusion_head --feedback-dir data/ton_iot/processed/step4_feedback_head15

limitations: Edges are aggregated with the attack label in the grouping key, so these are not deployment-valid estimates.
Macro-F1 is over 8 eval classes (dos and ransomware dropped for support); not comparable to the UNSW 10-class ladder.

The ladder does NOT hold. Nothing is significantly out of order except the GNN at the bottom: AGAF ties the LLM (CI crosses zero) and the loop ties AGAF (CI crosses zero). The intended strict order Loop > AGAF > {GNN, LLM} is not demonstrated.

AGAF's learned output gate stayed at its 0.95 initialisation (trained bias 2.9947 vs init 3.0), so AGAF defers ~95% to the trained LLM head and reproduces it almost class for class. Head fusion stopped AGAF from hurting; it did not make the GNN branch contribute.

Because the fused branch barely reaches the output, disabling the gate-entropy regulariser (--gate-entropy-lambda 0) produced bit-identical predictions. The entropy term is not what flattened the gate.
The graph has 2127 edges; rare eval classes have 12-35 edges, so single-seed differences between fusion mechanisms are not resolvable (see the 2026-08-17 report).
top_k_percent must be passed explicitly for ToN: with no selected_feedback_config.json in the output dir the loop silently falls back to 16.0, which is UNSW's selected value, not ToN's 15.0.
